symbols.name: ground set size
symbols.meaning: The number of elements in the ground set $[h]$, from which the triples are drawn.
symbols.quote: Fix $h$, the number of elements in the ground set $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$.

symbols.name: set of triples
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: A *triple* is a three-element subset of $[h]$, and $\mathcal{K}$ is the set of all triples.

symbols.name: bank index
symbols.meaning: An index $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ of one entry of a bank, a triple of triples.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of values indexed by $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathcal{K}^3$; the two banks are $X$ and $Y$, with entries $x_a$ and $y_a$.

symbols.name: source bank
symbols.meaning: One of the two banks of values, with entries $x_a$, that the network exchanges.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of values indexed by $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathcal{K}^3$; the two banks are $X$ and $Y$, with entries $x_a$ and $y_a$.

symbols.name: target bank
symbols.meaning: The other of the two banks of values, with entries $y_a$, that the network exchanges.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of values indexed by $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathcal{K}^3$; the two banks are $X$ and $Y$, with entries $x_a$ and $y_a$.

symbols.name: indicator vector
symbols.meaning: The $0/1$ vector of a triple $T$, with a $1$ in the coordinate of each element of $T$.
symbols.quote: For a triple $T$, its indicator vector $t_T$ is the $0/1$ vector on $[h]$ with a $1$ in the coordinate of each element $i$ of $T$ and $0$ elsewhere.

symbols.name: neighbouring triple
symbols.meaning: A triple that is a neighbour of the other triple $T$ when they share exactly one element.
symbols.quote: Two distinct triples $S$ and $T$ are *neighbours* when they share exactly one element.

symbols.name: neighbouring triple
symbols.meaning: A triple, here the triple whose indicator vector is $t_T$.
symbols.quote: For a triple $T$, its indicator vector $t_T$ is the $0/1$ vector on $[h]$ with a $1$ in the coordinate of each element $i$ of $T$ and $0$ elsewhere.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The auxiliary wire attached to an ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$.
symbols.quote: For each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ there is a side wire $A_{ST}$, and for each element $i\in[h]$ there is a central wire $C_i$.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The auxiliary wire attached to an element $i$ of the ground set.
symbols.quote: For each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ there is a side wire $A_{ST}$, and for each element $i\in[h]$ there is a central wire $C_i$.

symbols.name: ground element
symbols.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, one coordinate of an indicator vector.
symbols.quote: For a triple $T$, its indicator vector $t_T$ is the $0/1$ vector on $[h]$ with a $1$ in the coordinate of each element $i$ of $T$ and $0$ elsewhere.

relations.quote: Each gate is labelled by [Subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space, meaning one on which the form restricts to a nonsingular form, so that the whole space splits as the subspace plus its orthogonal complement.

relations.predicate: is built within the framework of
relations.quote: The network is built within the framework of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md): every wire is a role and every gate carries a frame, so the same scalar gates can act on arrays.
